description: Product-level deterministic simulation journeys covering economy/logistics/combat composition. Repeated textual simulation results (including the per-run `work` counter line) are the correctness gate; hosted-linux wall-clock timing is advisory. The stable deterministic work counters are declared as executable growth/budget contracts in `operations` and evaluated by `coding-tooling performance work` from the `performance:work` evidence collector (scripts/performance-work.sh, `raid-defense-sim --work-evidence`). The same shapes are enforced by crates/raid-defense-core/tests/scaling_contracts.rs and logistics_targeting_contracts.rs; reporting/determinism by crates/raid-defense-sim/tests/work_counters_report.rs.

scenarios.description: Run the balanced deterministic policy through economy growth, workers, construction, repeated waves and combat.
correctnessEvidence: byte-identical simulator report across repeated executions
full requested horizon or explicit deterministic town destruction
deterministic work counters identical across reruns

metrics.name: flow_field_rebuilds
metrics.notes: Grid-wide navigation computations (flow fields and from-scratch grid searches). Constant w.r.t. agent count under unchanged topology; topology/goal changes may rebuild per goal. Enforced by crates/raid-defense-core/tests/scaling_contracts.rs.

metrics.name: navigation_cells_visited
metrics.notes: Cells expanded by navigation rebuilds; at most one grid sweep per rebuild. Enforced by crates/raid-defense-core/tests/scaling_contracts.rs.

metrics.name: path_follow_steps
metrics.notes: Per-agent next-step lookups against retained navigation; may scale linearly with active agents.

metrics.name: target_candidate_evaluations
metrics.notes: Raider candidates examined by tower targeting; follows the local candidate set, not total raiders. Enforced by crates/raid-defense-core/tests/scaling_contracts.rs.

metrics.name: logistics_candidate_searches
metrics.notes: Worker/resource/storage/site candidates examined by logistics assignment, reported separately from path-follow work. Idle-worker assignment uses a per-tick candidate index, so searches follow assignments x relevant candidates plus one candidate sweep per tick, not idle-worker-ticks. Enforced by crates/raid-defense-core/tests/logistics_targeting_contracts.rs and the worker-logistics operation.

metrics.name: policy_validation_probes
metrics.notes: Candidate player commands validated by the headless policy.

metrics.name: world_clones
metrics.notes: Full game-state clones/materialisations made while probing candidate commands; must be 0 (no explicit O(N) clone contract).

operations.description: Advance 80 raid ticks under unchanged navigation topology with N slow, unkillable basic raiders on the field (economy paused, Town Hall cannot fall). Mirrors scaling_contracts.rs.

raiders.description: basic raiders alive and moving during the measured window

metrics.name: flow_field_rebuilds
metrics.notes: Retained navigation: no grid-wide rebuild while topology is unchanged, whatever the raider count.

metrics.name: navigation_cells_visited
metrics.notes: No navigation sweep while topology is unchanged.

metrics.name: path_follow_steps
metrics.notes: Per-agent next-step lookups against retained navigation; linear in active raiders.

operations.description: A level-1 arrow tower guards the north gate over a 22-tick window. Four near-stationary gate raiders (one inside the tower range) plus N-4 fast raiders walking away from it; targeting follows the local candidate set. Mirrors logistics_targeting_contracts.rs.

raiders.description: raiders alive in the wave; only the four gate raiders are local to the tower

metrics.name: target_candidate_evaluations
metrics.notes: Raider candidates examined by tower targeting; constant while only distant raiders grow.

operations.description: N workers run 1200 ticks of logistics over fixed, finite resources: every seeded forest holds two harvest batches and does not regrow inside the window, one sawmill, Town Hall storage only. Assignments are bounded by the fixed stock. Mirrors logistics_targeting_contracts.rs.

workers.description: people in the settlement (base capacity and starting people)

metrics.name: logistics_candidate_searches
metrics.notes: Candidates examined by logistics assignment and next-leg selection. Two points, so the linear bound is the ratio check: search work per worker must not grow with the crew. Idle workers re-scanning every candidate every tick would violate it.

operations.description: The worker-logistics settlement after its fixed stock is worked out (2400 warm-up ticks): every worker idles at the Town Hall with nothing assignable for 600 measured ticks.

workers.description: people in the settlement (base capacity and starting people)

metrics.name: logistics_candidate_searches
metrics.notes: The per-tick candidate index sweeps the relevant candidates once per tick, whatever the number of idle workers; an idle worker with nothing assignable examines no candidates.

operations.description: N workers haul wood for six open arrow-tower construction sites in the north while S settlement storage nodes exist (the stocked Town Hall plus S-1 empty Storage Houses in the south, farther from every site). Measured over the 8 ticks after every worker was assigned and before any returns idle, so the only logistics work is construction-source selection while hauling.

haulers.description: people in the settlement, all hauling for construction sites

storages.description: settlement storage nodes (Town Hall plus Storage Houses)

metrics.name: logistics_candidate_searches
metrics.notes: A hauler re-checks its construction source on every movement step toward it. The retained per-site source ranking stops at the first stocked, reachable node, so the work per step does not grow with the storage count; re-scanning every storage node each step would violate the constant bound.

operations.description: Run the balanced headless policy (seed 41) through economy growth, construction and waves for N ticks.

metrics.name: world_clones
metrics.notes: Candidate commands are validated against the authoritative state in place; no explicit O(N) clone contract exists.
